result.result:
Text pulled in with `.. include::` now goes through the `source-read` event, so in the issue's example both `&REPLACE_ME;` occurrences become `REPLACED`. The new test passes and fails without the fix. Nothing is committed.

**Cause:** Sphinx did fire `source-read` for `something-to-include.rst` when it read that file as its own document. But docutils' `include` directive reads the file from disk again and inserts the raw lines into the including document, so those edits never made it into `index.html`.

**Fix** (`Include.run` in `sphinx/directives/other.py`): when an extension is listening for `source-read`, the directive intercepts the step where docutils inserts the included lines. It fires `source-read` on that text and then inserts the modified version. It leaves out the end-of-inclusion marker that docutils adds, and puts things back once the directive finishes. With no listeners, nothing changes.

- **Nested includes** work, because each `include` gets the same treatment.
- **Non-document includes** (e.g. a `.txt` file) have no document name, so the extension gets the file path as `docname`. I chose that over passing `None`, which could break extensions that expect a string. Upstream Sphinx may pass `None` here instead.
- **Double handling:** an included `.rst` file that is also built as its own page now goes through `source-read` twice — once as its own page and once where it's included. Replacements like the Yocto ones still give the right result, but an extension that isn't safe to run twice on the same text could see a change.
- **Other cases:** `<std>`-style includes, `literalinclude`, and `include` with `:code:` or `:literal:` don't insert the text this way and are unchanged.

**Tests:** there is a new test root, `tests/roots/test-directive-include/` (with nested includes), and a new `test_include_source_read_event` in `tests/test_directive_other.py`. The first version of that test passed even without the fix: it searched the HTML for `&REPLACE_ME;`, which is written as `&REPLACE_ME;` in HTML. I rewrote the assertions.

I ran `tests/test_directive_other.py`, `test_directive_code.py`, `test_environment.py`, `test_build_html.py` and `test_util_rst.py`: 599 passed, 3 failed. The failures are `test_literal_include_linenos`, `test_linenothreshold` and `test_html_code_role`. They fail the same way with all my changes removed. I couldn't run ruff or mypy because neither is installed in `.venv`.

**Docs:** I added a `CHANGES` entry under 7.2.0 "Bugs fixed" and a note with `versionchanged:: 7.2` in `doc/extdev/appapi.rst`. The entry cites #10678 from memory; the issue text doesn't include the number, so please check it.
